I have written Shell in 42 public repositories, from 2013 to 2026; in 13 of them it is the main language.

What it was for: [Tools](@/projects/tools.md) (11), [Systems and infrastructure](@/projects/systems.md) (10), [Data and GIS](@/projects/data.md) (5) and [Media and art](@/projects/media.md) (5).

Most recently: [Kompendium](@/work/kompendium-epistemicke-anihilace.md): A book, a website and a wiki: mechanisms, detection signatures, defence and recovery, cross-linked into a graph you can explore; [Majordomus](@/work/prismatic-majordomus.md): One policy for every AI coding tool, scoped tasks with a finish contract, a mesh for many sessions and machines, and an integration queue that lands only verified work. Local; it never invokes a model; [Sonic Playground](@/work/sonic-playground.md): A hand-picked music blog built with Phoenix and Elixir on the Kita theme.

9 of these projects run as live sites.

I also used it in client work under confidentiality agreements. Roles: Architect, Lead engineer, AI engineer and Data engineer. What was solved: LLM agents, Decision support, AI transformation and Audit trail. The use cases below give the principle and the intent of that work; no client, person, date or number is named.

How to read the evidence: every [repository](@/glossary/repository.md) below is measured from GitHub and GitLab (every 6 hours) and says how it uses Shell: as the main language, as a measured share of its code, in its declared stack or as a topic. The reference graph links Shell to the repositories and to the other languages and technologies they use together.
